comment: The static cost function assigns one constant per straight-line region of the post-normalization canonical program. A region's constant counts its expression nodes and static-data value nodes (object keys count nothing). Invocation, branch, parameter-default, and builtin-call boundary nodes belong to no region; their charges arrive as events or as entry into the region they select. See docs/runtime/execution-limits.md.

cases.description: constant array program is one region counting the array node and its items
builtin call node is a boundary; its literal arguments form the entry region
function literal counts 1 where it is created; each $if arm is its own region
cases.comment: The body entry region counts the condition's $var and literal; the gt call and the $if node are boundaries.

cases.description: $let is not a region boundary: binding nodes fold into the containing region
cases.comment: Bindings are strict, so the body entry region counts the $let node, the binding's $var and literal, and the two $var reads in $in; the add and mul call nodes are builtin-call boundaries.

cases.description: $raw payload counts one per value node
cases.comment: Object 1 + grid array 1 + two row arrays 2 + four scalars 4 = 8. The $raw wrapper adds nothing.

cases.description: the equivalent plain constant data derives the same constant
a $let with no boundary inside folds entirely into its containing region
cases.comment: The body is one region despite the $let: the $let node 1, the binding's array node 1, its $var and literal 2, and the $var read in $in 1. No invocation, branch point, parameter-default boundary, or builtin call splits it.

cases.description: a positional $default is its own region behind the parameter-default boundary
cases.comment: The default expression's region counts the add call's two literals; the add call node is a builtin-call boundary. The body region counts the two $var reads. The parameter-default boundary is the only boundary an evaluation strategy could reach through; the region is entered by the default-force event.

cases.description: a multi-segment path is nested $get nodes, one count per segment
cases.comment: Three $get nodes plus the $var target: constant 4. Bare $get is straight-line work — no boundary, no event.

cases.description: a $get $else arm is its own region; the target and key stay in the containing region
cases.comment: The $get node with an $else arm is a branch point: the body region counts the $get node and the $var target, and the arm's literal forms the region entered by arm selection on a miss.

cases.description: capture-record entries count in the region containing the function literal
cases.comment: The inner literal captures a and b, so the body region counts the literal 1 plus one per record entry 2. Creation fires no event; the captured values are shared, charged where they were produced. The inner body region counts its array node and three $var reads.

cases.description: type annotations contribute zero to region constants
cases.comment: The $type and $returns payloads are static syntax that never produces a value — like object keys, unlike data literals. The constants are identical to the bare form of the same program: entry 1, body 2 (two $var reads; the mul call node is a boundary).

cases.description: a further $and operand is its own region entered by arm selection
cases.comment: The $and node is a branch point: the first operand evaluates unconditionally in the containing region, and each further operand is a region entered by continuing past a true operand. The boolean validation of each operand is a kind check folded into the node counts, not an event.
